newsitem.title: USA: NBC says signs Brokaw to five-year deal.
newsitem.headline: NBC says signs Brokaw to five-year deal.

text.p: NBC said Thursday it signed television news anchorman Tom Brokaw to a new five-year contract.

Terms were not disclosed. Published reports said Brokaw was offered about $7 million a year. A spokeswoman for NBC News declined to comment. However, a source at NBC familiar with the situation said the final figure was lower.

Under the deal, Brokaw continues as anchor and managing editor of "NBC Nightly News" and will continue to serve as contributing anchor to "Dateline NBC," the prime-time news magazine show, and programme anchor for MSNBC, its all-news cable channel that is a joint venture with Microsoft Corp.
Brokaw, who began his career at NBC as a reporter at KNBC-TV, its Los Angeles TV station, in 1966, was reportedly wooed by Time Warner Inc.'s Cable News Network, with an offer of $8 million a year.
NBC is owned by General Electric Co.
